title: Back before sunset
told: an old story of the Pythagoreans

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? is there someone who’d notice if you went quiet for a week?
options: then you’re rich. this story is about friends like that.
that’s honest. this one might help you find them.

steps.line: In ancient Syracuse lived two friends, Damon and Phintias. They were Pythagoreans, followers of the old teacher Pythagoras. Their saying: friends have all things in common.
The ruler, Dionysius, didn’t believe friendship like that was real. His courtiers said: let’s test it.
So Phintias was accused of plotting and sentenced to die. He asked for the rest of the day to put his affairs in order.

steps.q: Someone has to guarantee that Phintias will come back. What happens?
o: Damon offers to take his place
steps.why: Damon steps forward, without being asked.

steps.line: Damon stepped forward: if Phintias didn’t return, Damon would die in his place. The court laughed. Who comes back to die?

steps.q: What does the tyrant’s test quietly assume about people?
o: Anyone will save himself when it counts
Phintias really did plot against him
Damon secretly wants to die a hero
steps.why: Dionysius bet that under pressure, everyone looks out for himself. The Pythagoreans bet the other way, with a life on the table.

steps.line: The sun sank lower. And just before it set, Phintias came back.
Dionysius was stunned. He embraced them both, and begged to be let in as their third friend.

steps.q: How do we know this story at all? The ancient source says it came from…
o: Phintias, who wrote it down later
steps.why: The philosopher Aristoxenus said Dionysius told it to him in Corinth, after the tyrant had lost his throne. The man who set the test became the one who told it.

steps.line: Today: two old friends on a park bench at sunset, a small quarrel mended before dark. The kind of friend who comes back.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Phintias was free until sunset. He could have run. Why does his return matter as much as Damon’s offer?
o: Damon’s trust only worked if he kept faith
Guards were following him all day
He hoped the tyrant would pardon him
steps.why: Damon’s offer was brave, but it only meant something if Phintias came back. The friendship needed both of them.

say: here’s what i love. the test was meant to prove friendship was fake. it ended with the most powerful man in the city asking to be let in.

the pythagoreans lived as a community: shared meals, shared study, shared everything. they said friendship is equality. and they had a rule: if friends quarreled, they made up before the sun went down. you can’t walk this path alone. find your people.

steps.q: Dionysius had power, money and guards. Why did he still want what Damon and Phintias had?
o: He wanted to learn Pythagoras’s math
A friend who’d die for you can’t be bought
He planned to test them again later
steps.why: He could command anyone. He couldn’t command that.

today.say: today, keep the pythagorean rule: before the sun goes down, reach out to one friend. mend a small thing if there is one. if there isn’t, just tell them you’re glad they’re yours.
options: good. send it before sunset, before you talk yourself out of it.
they may be thinking of you too.

card.from: an old story of the Pythagoreans
card.keepWhy: A friend who comes back before sunset.
sources: Iamblichus, On the Pythagorean Life 233–236, citing Aristoxenus, who heard it from Dionysius himself in Corinth: courtiers claim Pythagorean loyalty is false; Phintias is accused of plotting and condemned; he asks for the rest of the day to settle his own and Damon’s affairs; Damon stands surety; the court mocks; Phintias returns at sunset; Dionysius embraces them and asks to be received as a third in their friendship.
Diodorus Siculus 10.4.3–6; Cicero, De Officiis 3.45 and Tusculan Disputations 5.63 (Dionysius asks to be admitted as a third friend).
Diogenes Laërtius 8.10 (Pythagoras, after Timaeus: friends have all things in common; friendship is equality).
Plutarch, On Brotherly Love 17 (Moralia 488B–C): the Pythagoreans, if anger led them to abuse each other, joined right hands and were reconciled before the sun set.
